en: The Sūtra on the Ten Auspiciousnesses Spoken by the Buddha;
the translator’s name is lost, now appended to the Qin Records.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in Rājagṛha, together with...
There was a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus, together with five thousand bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded before and behind by countless hundreds of thousands of people, preached the sūtra for them.

At that time, within the great assembly, there was a mahāsattva named Vimalavyūha. Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee upon the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If there are currently present Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and if there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha and hear their names, receive and uphold them, and recite them, would they swiftly attain non-retrogression from the unsurpassed, true, and correct path?”
The Buddha said to the Great Being Vimalavaiśaya: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son, it is well that you are able to ask such a question; it will bring great benefit. There is, noble son!

To the east, passing from here through as many Buddha-worlds as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world named Square Adornment (Dik-saṃbhūṣita). In that land there is a Buddha, named Great Radiance (Mahāprabhāsa) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, son of good family!
To the east, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of two Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Sarvajayottara. In that land there is a Buddha named Jñānapradīpa-prabhāsa Tathāgata."
There is a world named Vajra; in that land there is a Buddha named Mahāvīra Tathāgata.
There is a world named Pure Noble Abode; in that land there is a Buddha named Vimalaraja Tathāgata.
There is a world named Golden Light; in that land there is a Buddha named King of Ten Canopies of the Supreme Image Banner Tathāgata.
There is a world named Great Majestic Power; in that land there is a Buddha named Sovereign King of Majestic Power Tathāgata.
There is a world named Fragrant Incense; in that land there is a Buddha named King of Supreme Reflected Image Tathāgata.
There is a world named Jewel Adornment; in that land there is a Buddha named Inner Jewel Tathāgata.
There is a world named Sāgarapradīpa; in that land there is a Buddha named Mahāsāgara Tathāgata.
There is a world named Daśabalapradīpa; in that land there is a Buddha named Daśabaladarśin Tathāgata.

You should know, Vimalavaijayanta, that if a son or daughter of good family who seeks the Buddha-way were to take seven treasures filling as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand along the Ganges and offer them as alms to the Tathāgatas, the Perfectly Awakened Ones; yet if another son or daughter of good family, upon hearing the names of these Buddhas, were to receive, uphold, recite, and keep them in mind, and extensively explain them for others within the great assembly—the merit of this latter person would surpass the merit of the former.
Desiring further to explain the meaning, he spoke these verses:

"Even if one were to take the worlds of all Buddhas, as numerous as the sands along the Ganges, and fill them with the seven treasures to offer as a gift; yet if there should be one who hears the names of those Buddhas..."
With faith and joy, never forgetting, their merit shall surpass that of the former.
"If one hears the names of the Buddhas, reciting them without forgetfulness,
that person should not harbor doubt, saying, 'I shall not attain Buddhahood.'"
With the six supernormal powers inexhaustible, extending through incalculable kalpas,
his body shall be golden in color, adorned with the primary and secondary marks.
If one upholds the name of the Buddha, even after ten billion kalpas have passed,
"You shall swiftly attain perfect enlightenment.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Great Being Vimalacchattra, the various bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, spirits, and people of the world were all filled with joy and reverently accepted the Buddha’s teaching.
The Sutra on the Ten Auspiciousnesses Spoken by the Buddha
